utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, everyone. Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All the accused are present. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. -- I can't see behind these columns. Mr. Haynes, Mr. Bourgon, and I think that's it. The Prosecution, I notice Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Vanderpuye, and I don't think there is anyone else. Okay. The witness is already present in the courtroom. May I please remind you all the protective measures that we'd gone through yesterday so never refer to the witness by his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm happy to see you again. We are going to proceed with your testimony. May I just remind you of the solemn declaration that you made yesterday and which is still valid today. Mr. Meek, you still had the floor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Witness. How are you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: After we finish with this witness then there are a couple of decisions that we need to hand down, and if -- I didn't ask you if you have preliminaries, but if you have, they will no longer be preliminaries, they will come after we finish with the testimony. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Meek, and good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I just have a couple of questions. Were you armed or the other two individuals with you armed as you made your way to the free territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And when I say armed, I don't mean necessarily machine-guns, handguns, rifles, but grenades, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, do you know an individual by the name of Osman -- can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Go into private session. Osman is a very common name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I know that, so that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's like saying John or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I understand that but that was first name only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I hope you know the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Meek has finished his cross-examination for Accused Beara. Who is going next? Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm Jelena Nikolic, attorney-at-law, and I appear for Mr. Drago Nikolic in these proceedings. I have a few questions for you in relation to the events that you testified about yesterday. Do you remember that in 1996, on the 7th of July you saw investigators from the OTP once more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the people from The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From The Hague.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot confirm the date when this happened and what year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If there is a statement that you signed, do you accept that that is when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was the time when they showed you several photographs of different buildings and different places. Does this refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tell you they showed me all these things at that time. I cannot remember all of this exactly. You go on putting your questions and let's move on that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you met with the investigators of the OTP they showed you the pictures of a school and meadow and different places then, in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you were telling us about what had happened, you said that on the road to Krizevici you arrived during the night between the 13th and 14th of July, 1995, after midnight around 2.00 in the gym of a school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you were getting off the bus and as you were approaching that building --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: -- the soldiers made you look at your feet and it was night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The next day, as you said, around 2000 hours when you were taken out of the gym you were blindfolded; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So in fact you never saw the building of that school where you were for a while -- or, rather, in the gym of that school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when I didn't see it then after that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That night and the next day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that night I watched it all night when we were getting out of the gym and going onto the truck. That is when they blindfolded us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And during the night while you were in the gym, you were watching all of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Watching, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: However, while you were outside you couldn't see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for that, I could see, because it was see-through, this blindfold, and I put it up on my forehead, because being a disabled person I could trip over and fall, and when I can see properly then I can see and I won't fall.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And no one cautioned you because of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They just shouted, "Keep quiet. Don't talk." That was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could we please call up on e-court document -- or, rather, the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 7th of July, 1996, and the number is 5297. 5247 -- 3D247. Could we please see page 2. Sir, could you please be so kind as to look at the screen in front of you. It would be the third paragraph that starts with the words "I would not be capable of recognising."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would you please read this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot read it. I cannot see that right. Even with glasses it's hard for me to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can I read it out for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: "I would not be able to recognise this building as the school that I was taken to during the night between the 13th and 14th of July, 1996, because it was night-time and I had to watch my feet only." So in 1996 when you talked to the Office of the Prosecutor only a year after these events, you stated that you cannot recognise this building, and that was the picture of this school that was shown to you then, as the building where you were taken during that night in 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not recognise the school, but I could recognise the gym, especially the interior of the gym, because I had a good look at it. Schools were built according to the same system. There could be a similar school somewhere else, but the interior of the gym is the same one that I was in. When I saw that the school and the gym were linked up, then I realised that it was that same school that was there then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the case of most schools, are the gyms and the schools themselves linked up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P1775.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at this photograph in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Is that the gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now I cannot orient myself because I cannot see the door at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Is it quite different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's different because the roof construction is not like this. The windows are different on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you something else. It was your testimony that you spent the entire night in this gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And the prisoners --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not certain if I'm correct, but if my colleague is insinuating that the photograph that she's referred to the witness is the gym in which he spent the entire night, I don't think that it's a fair question or an appropriate question. I think it's been established for the record that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. My intention was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, because what I was going to say is precisely what Judge Prost has just told me, and I'm sure Judge Kwon would agree with this. I don't want this discussion to go any further in the presence of the witness. Okay. Do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Can you remove your headphones for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I can just move on and speak in my own bad English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's do that. You've said what you had to say. Do you want to expand on it, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I was just trying to catch up on the -- on the scrolling -- on the scrolling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You said it's not a fair question or an appropriate question if she is -- if Madam Nikolic is insinuating that the photograph she's referred the witness to is the gym in which he spent the entire night. That's what we have on the transcript. You kept on saying, "I think it has been established for the record that this is the case," and I stopped you there because you hadn't finished, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, actually what that should read is that that is not the case, and I have had a chance to read the transcript and I do stand by my objection. The witness did not identify that photograph as the gym in which he spent the night, and so I don't think it's an appropriate or fair question to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me hear what Madam Nikolic has to say. If you can address -- the point is --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's clear enough I don't need to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My intention was not to confuse the witness, just to show that the gym inside could be similar, but I don't want to put him -- for him to agree with me that he was in this particular gym which is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in any case, he hasn't agreed to that proposition, so I think we can move -- we can move --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can move. Thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. I think it was a storm in a teacup. Let's proceed with your next question, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to ask for this photograph to be removed from the screen, because I think that in his answers the witness is going to make references to the photograph and we don't really need that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Sir, when we started this part of our discussion, from midnight on when you came to this gym, some gym, you said that during the course of the night several prisoners would be brought in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to these men who were being brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to one of them, this person I knew. So I talked to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that some of these prisoners came in escorted by APCs of the UN, certain convoys, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just heard that they came on a truck, this person that I talked to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were there groups of prisoners who were brought in during the course of the afternoon on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something in relation to the photograph that my colleague showed you yesterday. If you remember -- we don't really have to look at it on the screen again if you think it's all right. The photograph where you saw the iron railing and the railroad. Do you remember that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On another occasion when you met with the OTP in 1998 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: -- this is what you said when you described the place where it was that you were lying --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm reading to you the notes of the investigator of the OTP. "Nearby he saw some railing and a railroad, but he could --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak slower -- read slower, rather.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: "Nearby he saw some railing and a bridge, but he did not see a railroad. Next to the meadow he saw a house and tall trees between two heaps of bodies, as well as an excavator that could rotate 360 degrees." Sir, what I read out to you just now was recorded by an investigator of The Hague Tribunal as a result of his conversation with you in October 1998. So on the basis of what you told him and that he wrote down, you said that you saw a house by the meadow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Underneath those pastures there was a house, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P1706.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Now you're going to see a photograph on your screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So I'd like to ask you whether that is, perhaps, the house and the meadow that you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Now I cannot remember this because it was a long time ago, but it looked like -- I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness 1706, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 1706.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. 1705 then. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Sir, can this photograph refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In fact, yesterday when testified about the location where you were lying down on the 14th of July in the evening, you described it and recognised it from what people from Tuzla told you when you arrived on free territory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised it was a railroad and the flyover. They recognise it by the flyover, and they recognise it by -- as the gym where they used to play basketball.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And who are these people from Tuzla who refreshed your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people from that place who were living there, who had been expelled to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And they were present while you were giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And when did they describe that location to you, the location where you were lying down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four years later, I can't remember when I heard that, but I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, madam. Mr. Lazarevic or Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Miodrag Stojanovic and together with my colleagues here I appear for Mr. Borovcanin. I'd only like to go through a couple of documents with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We have to talk a bit slower, because it seems that we are fast talkers, both of us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'll slow down a little then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well yesterday, on the 11th of July in the afternoon you were in your village, engaged in your usual farming works.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Also yesterday, for the record it's transcript page 32, lines 13 to 16, you also said at one point you heard a report from your locals that somebody from the civilian defence had come to pass on the message that all the population should go to Potocari except able-bodied men fit for the army who should go through the woods.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us go through this in detail. Can we look at Exhibit 1D0041. While we're waiting for it, I would like to say that is your statement that you had given to the Prosecutor -- to the Office of the Prosecutor, the investigator Jean-Rene Ruez, in July 1995, and on page -- I have just been told that the number is not right. 1D00441. Thank you. In that statement when you were describing this moment -- can we see the first paragraph of page 2 both in English and in Serbian. You said, among other things -- I will read it because you can't see well. You say, speaking of this event: "Around 1600 hours a soldier came and asked all able-bodied men to go to the front line. I did not go because I was an invalid." And then you go on to say: "Between 1800 hours and 1900 hours another soldier came and said they were breaking out through the front line and that all able-bodied men should try to save themselves, whereas the other -- the rest of the population should go to the UNPROFOR base in Potocari."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But can we agree that this is a bit different now? Once you said a man from the civilian defence came, and the first time, in 1995, you said that one soldier came, then another one, and said the people should go.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I'm not denying the statement I had given earlier. But regardless of whether it was a civilian or a soldier, somebody came and said that Srebrenica had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it's possible that a soldier came on two occasions to pass that message.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the person was able-bodied, he could have been a soldier, but he could have been from the civilian defence equally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, and that's why I wanted to remove this ambiguity. But what I want to ask you is do you remember -- did they tell you then when you said the civilian population should go to Potocari, did they tell you then that you would be transported from there to Tuzla, Kladanj, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said transportation would be there, but they didn't say where. They said that those of us who were not able bodied, fit for the army, would go on from Potocari somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify. That piece of information that you would go to Tuzla with somebody who would organise the transport, that's something you were told in the afternoon of the 11th of July. Could it have been between the -- between 6.00 and 7.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From this statement I see that your son was living with you at the time. He was 30 then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And he left with the army, with the troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know to which military unit he belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know these things so well as to be able to say. I can tell you that it was a military unit in Srebrenica but no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he arrive in Tuzla? Did he get there to the territory under the control of the 2nd Corps? Did he arrive before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And if I'm not mistaken, you arrived on the 20th or the 21st of July, 1995. You were not able to say precisely.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a Wednesday, the 19th. I'm not sure though. At any rate, I did cross over several days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So on the 18th of -- or 19th of July -- on that day in July, around 18 or 1900 hours around your village, Ornica, you didn't see any Serbian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we have to wait for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right. It's all right. Let's take it easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That decision to go to Potocari, and I mean the civilian population, the people who were able bodied should go to the woods, that was a decision of the authorities in the enclave, and who passed that message on to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't even at home. I don't know who had come to tell us. I just came home when they called out to me to come back. I dropped the work I was doing gathering hay and came back home, and they told me -- my folks told me that somebody had come to say that Srebrenica had fallen, that the population who was not able bodied, not fit for the army, should go to the base in Potocari, and able-bodied men should go through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now knowing the terrain a little bit, would I be right in saying that you were going on foot from your hamlet or from your village through Lehorici, Milacevici, the area of upper Potocari, and you would come to Donji Potok?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that took you at least three hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the way, did you run into members of the 28th Division of the ABH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We only came across people who were going to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As you were descending towards the asphalt road leading to Srebrenica and Bratunac, on that intersection did you also see a group of APCs of the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see them, but I can't remember exactly where, at which point, whether it was as I was climbing down towards the asphalt road, whether they were down there or at an elevation, and I can't tell you how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because we had occasion to hear testimony here saying that they had made a check-point on the way from their base to Srebrenica and that there were four APCs stationed there on the 11th of July. Could that be true according to your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was night and I wasn't looking around. I was just going towards the UNPROFOR base. But in the morning I saw that there was an APC or two, or maybe more. I can't confirm that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on. On that night of the 11th you were in Potocari. You spent the night outside the factory that you called Sacmara. Could we now look at an exhibit that I was told would take a long time to open, that's P02103, page 7 -- or photograph number 7. That's one of the photographs from the collection we received during the testimony of Jean-Rene Ruez, and it depicts a broader view of this village Donji Potocari. And, Witness, when you see the picture of Potocari, could I ask you to mark the place where you were outside that factory to the best of your recollection. You will see it on the screen in front of you. And could I ask the usher to give the witness a pen to do the marking. Could we zoom in a little to make it easier for the witness to mark the place? Thank you. Sir, we'll now give you a pen, and if you can find your way around this photograph, could you please mark the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I spent the night?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This blue frame marks the UN base. In the lower part of the picture you see the road leading to Srebrenica, and in the upper right corner you see the part of the road leading towards Bratunac. Is that the way you remember it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't orient myself here. Where is Srebrenica here?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the road going from Potocari, this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not the road coming from Potocari. It would be a little lower, in the lower left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, sorry for interrupting you. Could the registrar just point the cursor to the bottom of the screen, left-hand corner, on the road. On the road. Yes. Okay. Sir, do you see a kind of a lens moving on the screen? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is the road which takes you to Srebrenica. Now, could we move --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This thing up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This thing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rather, down there. Would that be Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is the road --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this goes to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And -- no. If you move the cursor now to the top right-hand corner. As the cursor moves, that is the road which would take you to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you orient --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Right. It has to be a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But do you orient yourself better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I can do it now, yes. Now I can find my way around. As long as you showed me which road leads to Bratunac. I couldn't remember before, but now I'm all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I now ask you, Witness, to take a pen and to mark the area outside the factory you call Sacmara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will be given a pen now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be here approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you can, on this map mark the place where the members of the Dutch Battalion were located who were releasing the buses, letting them go through. Put a line there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you mark the place on this map where that unfinished house that you mentioned was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I can't be sure -- I can't remember, but it should be -- since we were going this way towards the roadblock, and as we passed it, as we separated, it should be in the direction of this house. Between these two houses somewhere. I'm not sure, but it's possibly these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We also think it's there somewhere. But above those three dots where you marked that house, could you put the letters NK, which stands for unfinished house in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now where you marked the Sacmara factory, could you put a date 11-12/7/95. 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Thank you. And somewhere towards the bottom under that line on the road that you marked, could you put the letter P.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: P?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for "check-point."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And to finish with this, put today's date in the right bottom corner, 2nd November 2007, and above that put PW-169.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I do have some more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, but I've been educated to say thank you several times during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going to do that any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that all of this is in Donji Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All of it is in Donji Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Shall we agree that there is also a village called Gornji Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't need the usher's assistance any more. I have some more questions for the witness now. Yesterday during your examination-in-chief you said, among other things, that on the 12th of July in the morning, a delegation of the refugeed people came to the gates of the UNPROFOR base and asked them what was going to happen with you and when the evacuation would start. For the record it's page 35 of yesterday's transcript. And you were told that they were waiting for the buses, for your transport.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that your representatives or your delegates received this information from the members of the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would I be right in saying that it was in the morning at 7.00 or 8.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been at 10.00 in the morning, but at any rate it was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But in any case as you said yesterday, it was before the first Serb soldiers appeared.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Around what time, to the best of your knowledge, because you said something about that in your earlier statements and testimony. Around what time did your family move towards the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After all this time I can't remember the hours, but I can confirm the earlier statement I've given, because my memory was better then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's how I'm going to ask you. Don't hold it against me. You said it was between 4.00 and 6.00 on the 12th. 4.00 and 6.00 on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the Dutch Battalion were already around you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 36 of yesterday's transcript you said that those members of the UNPROFOR made some sort of human shield, a live fence to sort of streamline you towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so that we wouldn't rush as a crowd, that we would go as a -- in a column.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We had one witness testifying here, a witness who had been in Potocari on the same day as you among the refugeed people, and that witness said the soldiers were on the road, one Dutch soldier, one Serb, then one Dutchman, one Serb holding hands, and they let people through towards the buses by raising their arms to let people go through towards buses and lorries, whereas the Serb soldiers standing next to the buses separated men from their families. That was on the 6th of November, 2006, pages 3620 to 3630. And my question to you is: Was that witness right in describing how this evacuation took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people who were forming a chain, I didn't know any of them. They were all in uniform. So I suppose they were Dutch soldiers. But as we were passing through and as they began to separate us, I noticed, I saw that they were Serb soldiers. They were not raising arms when I was passing through. Instead, they narrowed the road down to a passage of about two metres so that people would go through it like a corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it's possible that it happened this way, too, as this other witness described it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know any of the soldiers. I thought they were all from the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you got onto the buses, I'm talking about you personally and your experience, you did not see any physical assaults, anyone beating anyone with rifle butts, anyone kicking or punching anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were there did you see anyone attack a member of the UNPROFOR, taking their equipment, their weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: These members of the Dutch Battalion, could they see this separation in front of the buses and the trucks that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, absolutely. They were turning around, and they saw who the Serb soldiers were separating from who.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did they react? Did they do anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. They were just looking, watching, and they were holding hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After they singled you out, they took you to this unfinished house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will we agree that this was a single-storey house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just one storey above the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the woodwork in place already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at P02103. That is the next photograph, page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, again I'm going to ask you to take a look at this. It will be in front of you. You will see a building, and I'm going to ask you whether it's that particular building or another one, if you can remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. Fine. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps this is going to take a while.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you to have a look at this. Let's have a look at it together. Do you see this house in the central part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will we agree that that's not the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's not the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to move on. While you were in the house that you were talking about --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- was there any mention of the members of the Serb army wishing to carry out an investigation as to whether there was anyone among you who had committed some war crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In conclusion, I'd like to ask you just one more thing. When you set out from this house --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- you said that you walked. You went on foot about 200 metres --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- across a field, a meadow. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right if I were to say on the basis of your previous statement that you arrived in Bratunac around 2200 hours, or, rather, 10.00 that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will we agree that your transport from the place where you boarded the buses to this hangar that you talked about could have taken up to 20 minutes at a maximum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than that. That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the moment when you boarded these buses nobody took away your rucksacks, the food that you had in these rucksacks, your equipment, nothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We had occasion here to hear testimony from a man who was similar to you who said that it was only before the school -- well, you said that you did not have a bag, but those who had bags left them in front of the school, the bags where they had food. Would that be correct as you remember it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was in front of the Vuk Karadzic school that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your recollection, that people who had rucksacks, bags with food inside left them outside before they entered the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was only in the morning that they took it away. When dawn broke, that's when they took away all our things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me finish with this: Will you agree that it was already dark when you set out towards Bratunac from Donji Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday when you testified about the tragic events that you were part of, you said that before it got dark at the place where this execution took place you said that you saw Mladic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, it is page 64 and page 65 of yesterday's transcript. Can you tell us what the approximate time was when General Mladic came to this meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot because I was so afraid then. I didn't know anything about what time it was, but I saw him very well. It was just before dark, and I saw him very well and this soldier who was escorting the little TAM truck, in the red car. They got out together. The solder was taller than Mladic, perhaps, say, a head taller than him, in grey uniform. He did not have a camouflage uniform, a grey uniform. This soldier had a grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's try to agree on something at least. Can we say that it was in the late afternoon hours of the 14th of July or in the evening hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that there is a statement given to the investigators of the Tribunal by Carl Bildt, who at that time was the special envoy of the General-Secretary of the UN in Bosnia and for the Balkans, and that he said that on that day, Friday the 14th of July, 1995, in Dobanovci near Belgrade in the evening he was attending a meeting with Slobodan Milosevic and General Mladic, would that bring into question this part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You stand by what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still claim I would lay my life for that. I saw him, that's for sure. You can check this. Had somebody taken a picture, then we could have a look at it. I tell you, I mean now I would lay my life to support that. Just like Carl Bildt is Carl Bildt, Mladic is Mladic. I tell you, no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now I thank you even more, Mr. Stojanovic. Witness, keep -- keep cool. Keep calm, okay? There is no reason to get keyed up about anything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this upsets me, this untruth, when such a high official like Carl Bildt can say something like that. How can I expect him to say something like that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have to be like us, very patient.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not get nervous if it was an illiterate person who said something like that or one of these people over there said something like that, that Mladic was in Belgrade, but Carl Bildt, to say something like that, shame on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll convey the message. So keep calm. Don't worry about anything. Lawyers are here to put questions, and everyone is trying to -- stop. Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine as far as all of them are concerned. They're not upsetting me at all. It's not the gentleman, the lawyer that upset me, no way. It's Bildt who upset me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I said, we'll make that sure he gets the message. Madam Fauveau. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir, my name is Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic, and I represent Radivoje Miletic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You were talking about a decision that was taken on the 11th of July, 2007, according to which people were to go to Potocari. If I understood you correctly even before arriving to Potocari in the afternoon of the 11th of July, 1995, you knew very well that the civilian population was going to be evacuated; that is right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you went to Potocari with the members of your family in order to be brought onto the territory that was under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said today on page 16, line 11, that before your departure for Potocari you had not seen Serb soldiers in your village, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in fact, during that road that brings you to Potocari, you never saw any Serb soldiers? And it was not the Serbs that told you to go to Potocari and to leave your homes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In that night, during that night that you spent in Potocari, and I'm talking about the night of the 11th and 12 July 1995, you never heard any gunshots, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in the morning of the 12th of July while you were in Potocari, there were no gunshots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Gunshots could be heard in the surrounding hills. Few and far between, and they were far away from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said yesterday on page 38 of the transcript that you were able to see that your family was going onto the buses. Is it right to say that your family was very well evacuated and they arrived on the territory that was under the control of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: My colleague asked you some questions regarding men, and you told him that before you arrived to the buses you had not seen if men were beaten. I just wanted to clarify something. After you were separated you did not also see if these men that got separated were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You were talking yesterday about an officer who came to speak to you while you were in that house in Potocari. You also told us that that man asked you why you chose Alija Izetbegovic instead of following Fikret Abdic. That was yesterday on page 40 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And Fikret Abdic is a Muslim, a Bosnian Muslim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And he was a political opponent of Alija Izetbegovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Later on that's the way it turned out to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about Bratunac. When you arrived in that hangar in Bratunac, you were amongst the first group that went into the hangar. And when you went inside the hangar, where were you? Were you at the end of the hangar or were you near the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the left-hand side, left of the entrance door. Perhaps a few metres away from the door on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when new groups arrived in that hangar were you pushed towards the -- the end, towards the -- towards the wall of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me. It was those in the middle. I remained by the wall on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And from where you were standing were you able to see the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that approximately 40 men were chosen during the night. It was on page 48 of the transcript. And you also told us that you did not count. How did you come to that figure of 40 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly. I always said that I never did any counting. I just guess it was about 40.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said yesterday on page 49 that one of the men that was selected was Ibran Papic -- Tabic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter isn't sure that she heard the name correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: To make sure that the name is correctly written on the transcript on page 14 it's Ibran, I-b-r-a-n, Mustafic, M-u-s-t-a-p-i-c [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've also told us that Ibran Mustafic had not come back to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember when you gave your first statement to the Bosnian authorities on the 21st of July, 1995, you said that Ibran Mustafic had been killed with a blunt object.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that. I remember I said that they quarrelled fiercely and then it all went quiet and he didn't come back. And then they asked me, "What do you think happened to him?" And I said that I think that the same thing happened to him that had happened to the other one. That is what my assumption was because he never came back. I just mentioned two cases that I knew of, how these people had been killed. Some were killed -- were hit with blunt objects. Others -- well, some people were heard -- or, rather, their beatings were heard, and others were not. So I just know of two particular cases how these people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown -- could the witness be shown 1D439. It's the statement of the 21st of July, 1995, given to the Bosnian authorities. Could the witness be shown page 2, please. Sir, I know that it's not easy for you to read, so I'm going to read you this passage in English, and it will be translated to you into B/C/S. You stated the following: [In English] "Ibran Mustafic, son of Mujo, from Potocari former head of Srebrenica municipality, who was killed with a blunt object." [Interpretation] You were talking about those two people, Ibran Mustafic was one of these two people that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But, sir, in this statement you mentioned, didn't you, Ahmet -- Hamed Efendic and Ibran Mustafic. Now, when we're talking about Ibran Mustafic, he's still alive, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And regard to these other men, the other 40 men that you had seen, you did not witness any executions regarding those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just saw how one of them was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And can you tell me when did you see that man that was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next morning when they told us that we could use one particular room as a toilet, we got out of that gym, went right to the toilet, and to the left-hand side they were taking people who were being singled out and killed. And then they told us that we shouldn't look left, that we should only look right. As I went out to go to the toilet and as I went back, from the column that was going to the toilet they took one man by shoulder and said, "You come here." Then I looked, and on one side it was either three or four men standing there, Serb soldiers, that is, and on the other side I think two. In front of them there was this one man with an automatic rifle facing the door of the warehouse, and he was shouting to this man. He said, "Come to me. Come to me." He walked between those soldiers, went towards the man with the automatic rifle, the one holding the automatic rifle. The one on the left-hand side hit him with an iron bar in the chest. He fell. The other one from the left-hand side hit him on the back with an axe. He fell on his belly and he was hit by this axe. He couldn't get the axe out or -- he couldn't get the axe out. And that's when I went back to the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, that was the next day, but during the night you didn't see anybody get killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just heard Hamed Efendic when three or four bullets were fired and somebody out there said, "He's done in. Drag him away."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: My question -- sir, my question was to know if you see if somebody got killed during the night from the 12th to the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see anything, but I heard the screams and moans and realised that people were being killed. I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you also said that Ibran Mustafic was killed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that, because no one came back alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I object to the question. I think that first it's been asked and answered. Second, counsel is implying that that is the only statement that the witness has made regarding that particular person, and I don't -- it is not, and for that reason I think that the question is inappropriate and also the inference that she's implying is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, do you wish to comment on that? Or move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in fact, sir, Your Honour, it is not the only declaration. I know there were a few statements, rather, and this was in the first statement, and rather I think that it would be more appropriate to continue this discussion either in the absence of the witness or if I would be allowed to just put my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead with your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, is it right to say that in fact you thought that these men were killed because they never came back to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can say that. That's why I assumed that Ibran Mustafic had been killed, because he did not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And also this goes for the same other 40 men. You thought that they were killed because they never came back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you thought that you arrived on the territory under the control of the ABiH on the 19th of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but there's no interpretation of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I will repeat the question, because your answer was not put down in the transcript. Is it right to say that in fact you said that these 40 men were killed because they never came back to the hangar? That's why you think so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you arrived on the territory under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 19th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, but the first statement would be correct if I'm making a mistake now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in fact, in your statement of the 25th of July, you said that you got there on the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, that's what I'm saying. I always say that. I could not be sure of the time. At any rate, I got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. But you gave your first statement to the Bosnian authorities on the 21st of July, 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Possibly. I'm not saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In any case, it was not long after your arrival on the territory controlled by the Bosnian authorities. Can we say that when you made that first statement that you were in a state of shock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably I was not quite myself then.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And during this first interview you talked about the events the way you think they occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in fact, after that every time you gave a subsequent statement you were always shown the first statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you arrived here to testify - I think that that was on the 30th of October - you had a meeting with someone from the OTP and they showed you your prior statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have approximately five more minutes. I don't know if you would like me to finish now or to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not the last one to cross-examine the witness, so we might take the break now, 25 minutes. It will also give the gentleman a well-deserved rest. You will have 25 minutes. Do you think that is enough for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: There won't be any further cross-examination unless my friend Mr. Sarapa has any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Sarapa, are you -- will you be cross-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No, I don't intend to ask him anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you have any re-examination, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I don't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then I suggest we go on for the next five minutes, but I want to make sure that everyone is in agreement. Yes, okay. Yes, Madam Fauveau. Sir, look at me. Look at me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm looking at you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not going to have the 25-minute break now. We are going to continue for another five minutes with further questions, and then I'm going to give you a much longer break, because you can go back home straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm -- great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like the witness to be shown Exhibit 5D483.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It's a statement in English, and I'll read the relevant portions out to you. This is information that derives from a meeting you had with the OTP, and what we can see here is that you were provided copies of your prior statements, a statement you made to the OTP on the 12th of August, 1995; another statement you made to the police of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 21st of July, 1995; another one you made to the police on the 25th of July, 1995; another statement you made to the OTP on the 7th of July, 1996; and finally, your transcript of -- the transcript of your testimony in the Karadzic and Mladic case on the 4th of July, 1996. And then you stated that these statements were correct, substantively correct. Do you remember stating that three days ago, on the 30th of October, 2007, last Tuesday? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, 12 years have elapsed since these events. Could we say when you testify here today you testify on the basis of your prior statements rather than the basis of your recollection of these events today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I pointed out that I cannot remember time periods in terms of what happened when, but I remember very well in my heart what it was that happened. Not at what time it happened, what kind of atrocious crime was committed against us innocent people, including myself, disabled. That I will never forget. I would rather forget my own name but not that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell me how you found out and why you stated that Ibran Mustafic had been killed by a blunt object? You stated that on the 21st of July, 1995, to the Bosnian police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were asking me whether he was killed with a firearm. I said no. What was he killed with? Well, he didn't come back and then I said most probably with a blunt object since I didn't hear how it was that he had been killed. He didn't come back. So then according to these other assumptions, well, what happened to those other men -- if you were to give me some other names of other people who survived from there, I'd really like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you acknowledge today that the statements you made about this particular person were not truthful?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. Sir. Sir, can you remove your headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I object to the question as to the characterisation of the statement. I don't know if it's a translation error and there's a difference between the statement being accurate and the statement being truthful, and I don't think counsel has established the necessary foundation to pose the question, and I don't think it's a proper question as it's been presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This time I wasn't following Madam Fauveau in French, so I can't tell you whether had -- what word she used and whether that interpretation is correct or not, but of course there is a big difference between a statement being accurate and another one being truthful or untruthful.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there is no translation error. I used word "truthful." "Veridique" in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think in that case the question's already been asked and answered. She's posed it. I can't see the entire transcript from here, but I think maybe two pages up. He was asked specifically the circumstances under which he made the statement and he answered the question. He said he presumed that the person had been killed based upon the fact that he didn't come back, and based upon the fact that he heard moaning and -- and other sounds of -- of injury.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we are talking about different things. I'm mentioning the first statement. In the first statement there are no hypothesis. The witness states that Mr. Mustafic was killed, even describes the killing. So now I'm asking him a question. I'm asking him whether he recognises or whether acknowledges that part of his statement was not truthful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But again, "truthful" is -- I want to make sure that we are on the same wavelength here, that "truthful" has a connotation of an intent and a determination not to speak out the truth, not to tell the truth. This is why I made the distinction before between whether it is a correct statement, whether it is accurate, or whether it is truthful. That's a completely different matter. You're suggesting -- as it is, you're suggesting to the witness that he deliberately lied. I think -- one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not suggesting that he deliberately lied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's hear what you have to say, and then we'll decide, Madam Fauveau. No. She was -- I stopped her. Oh, okay. You're not suggesting that he deliberately lied. I hadn't noticed that because I was -- all right. Then put the question, please. And I would suggest in putting the question that you make it clear to him that you're not imputing any malice on his part in withholding or twisting the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise today that the statement you made on the 21st of July, 1995, regarding Ibran Mustafic does not correspond to the truth, does not reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. You're still without re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Kwon, do you have ...? Judge Prost? I don't have any questions either. Before the gentleman leaves the courtroom, I forgot again this morning to confirm that we are sitting today being a Friday pursuant to Rule 15 bis because Judge Stole couldn't be with us and that has a retroactive effect from the beginning of the sitting. Sir, you've lasted much less than many other witnesses that have come here. We're finished with your testimony, which means that you are free to go. However, you will -- when you leave the courtroom, you are going to be assisted by our staff who will facilitate your return back home. On behalf of my colleagues and also on behalf of the Tribunal, I would like to thank you very much for having come over to give testimony on these events, and on behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And may you be well, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Now we will have the break. Then you need to tell me what's going to happen now. Before the break I would like to know what's going to happen afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have -- Mr. Blaszczyk is ready to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. No, no, because our intention was certainly not to waste the rest of the morning, so I'm glad you have talked about Mr. -- filling the gap.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, he's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let me follow you from my list, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have 65 ter 1693, 1698, 1707, and P02932. That's under seal. It's the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections? All right. The last one will remain under seal. And the rest, there being no objections, will be admitted. The Nikolic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just one document. P1705 that was shown to the witness, because 1706 has already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There's no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it is admitted. Borovcanin Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one exhibit. That's 4D IC186. That's the photograph that was marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document is so admitted. Madam Nikolic, to come back to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sorry, I inversed the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Although you stated that 1706 has already been admitted, I'm informed that it hasn't. So you --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted the reverse. 1705 has already been admitted into evidence, and I want to tender 1706. I'm sorry, I was wrong about the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's what I was saying. So 1706 is being admitted, and her request for the admission of 1705 is dropped, and therefore the previous ruling that 1705 was being admitted becomes moot and is also reversed. Okay. Now, I told you in the beginning of the sitting that we would proceed first with the testimony of the previous witness and that we'll come to the preliminaries afterwards. Are there any preliminaries? Yes, Mr. McCloskey. And decide whether we stay in open session or we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can be in open session for this. Mr. President, as you are, I think, aware, about two weeks ago we had a proofing session with Momir Nikolic. Julian Nicholls met with him. And from that proofing session it has arisen that Momir Nikolic has become adverse to the Prosecution's case. He made statements at that proofing session that we don't believe are credible and in reviewing his overall situation we have decided on balance to withdraw him as a witness. I've been mentioning that to Defence counsel. Now, of course should you be interested in hearing from Momir Nikolic, we will -- we are certainly able and willing to call him and lead him should you decide you would like to hear from him, but on balance we have decided that -- that he does not -- is not necessary for the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Having got accustomed to us, I can imagine that you can imagine our enthusiasm for that. Anyway, thank you for the information, which leads to the first conclusion, basically, and that is the Beara confidential motion, which doesn't need to remain confidential at this stage requesting disclosure of Momir Nikolic's personal notes, that becomes moot once he's not coming over to give testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. My question, of course, was directed to you, Mr. Ostojic, in particular, whether you consider this motion of yours moot now that the Prosecution does not intend to bring forward this witness although that has to be blessed by us before it becomes final.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning and thank you, Mr. President. I don't believe that it's moot; I think the Court should still grant my request on the motion and I also would like to inquire further on the comments made by my learned friend. He makes three specific comments: One, that the testimony of Mr. Momir Nikolic seems, according to him, to be adverse. I'd like for him to expand on that for me; also, he concludes for some reason without any basis that he believes the testimony now is "not credible" or "we don't believe it's credible"; and then three, he says doesn't think it's necessary for the OTP's case.
