utterances.text: What is a EOD?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is the team, IFOR team for checking, you know, the materials for explosives -- explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, on this Exhibit P02807, if I could direct your attention to that and if we could have that up on the e-court, please. And I'll just ask the question -- by the time it comes up I'm sure you'll be familiar with it. It says that Mr. Tollefsen actually EOD'd the 16 boxes of documents.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: It's mean that this -- one second. I have too big picture of this. Yeah, it's mean that boxes were checked by IFOR team for possible explosive material which could be located in these boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So that's what EOD means?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And at no time did you do an inventory in December and at no time did Mr. Tollefsen do an inventory of these documents other than the general size of the documents or the description of these documents and the number of the documents; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The contents were first reviewed when, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The contents of its collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the Drina Corps collection, though; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I mean, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. So -- I just don't want to be confused when you say each collection because I know you're going to be with us several more -- or a couple more times about other collections but I'm just focusing basically on the Drina Corps collection today.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: As I told before, the initial assessment I made in Zagreb it was very, very brief one, very rough one. I had a chance only to concentrate on few documents which I -- I noticed that were from July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Share with us, if you will, the actual place where the documents were from 1998 up until they arrived in Banja Luka in 2004. Do you know what that, basically, time line is, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. In -- I got this information from -- from few documents and from few statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you could be kind enough to identify it for us. Not to verify it but just so that we can be also informed as you are. From what documents and what statements?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: From documents received from the authority of Republika Srpska, mainly from ministry of interior of Republika Srpska, and then from the statement of Nebojsa Vukicevic and also from statement, (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know, sir, when you first started working on the Srebrenica unit, you knew that Srebrenica actually involved the area of Zvornik; correct? In part.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you learned that from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry to rush through it with you but we'll take our time and I apologise again to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you know -- did it ever cross your mind or did you ever question why the documents were brought back to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you the only one in the entire OTP or Srebrenica investigative team who wondered about that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: No, not -- not only me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me what actions you proposed or took to try to determine how was it that these documents that involved Zvornik ended up back at Zvornik. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I -- I did personally nothing, but I know that my colleagues from other teams who used to work also for Srebrenica team, they -- they made lot of efforts to -- to find out where the collection is located and how to get it back to -- to ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can't read it on the transcript because it's stalled on me, but what other -- what other people are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I'm referring to people who used to work for Srebrenica team and now they are working for another team.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who are they?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is investigator Brett Randall. He made a lot of efforts to locate this archive. He sent a lot of requests to the authorities of Republika Srpska as far as I know also to the Serbia and Montenegro to locate the location of this archive, not only this one but also the archive of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anyone else other than Brett Randall? You said people, and I just assumed it might be plural?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I think other -- other people were involved also in this -- this project, but I don't recall the names right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you remember, I'm sure you do, who Dragan Obrenovic's investigator was on his Defence team; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was his brother; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know, sir, why the documents were moved from Zvornik to Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Probably to avoid situation that the documentation at that time can be seized by SFOR or ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who do you think -- I mean we can't figure out who had the documents in Zvornik in 1998, but maybe you can help me. Did you ever find out who actually made the decision to transfer those documents from Zvornik to Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who, (redacted) I know that the decision was made by Svetozar Andric, the commander of the 5th or the chief of staff of the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That he made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ostojic. Let's go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, just very quickly in the time that we have. You don't know who maintained custody of the documents once they were transferred from Zvornik to Mali Zvornik. Do you know who had access to the documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Once they were transferred to Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I learned --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. I learned that access to these documents had Dragan Obrenovic, General Krstic, and General Miletic. At least I know these -- these three persons. They had access to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you, anyone else, did they have access to it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know, sir, who other than Dragan Obrenovic had access to the Drina Corps collection for the one year or close to one year, from April 1998 through March of 1999, while they were in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think it was Defence of the General Krstic, probably, General Miletic, and Dragan Obrenovic, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what's the basis of your knowledge of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: It is also from a statement of Dusan Vucetic and Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that I'm clear I have Nebojsa, not Dusan?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Nebojsa, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay. Did he give -- did he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification for my friend's question about the documents, the question being in Zvornik. They weren't stored in Zvornik, I don't think he's saying. They went through Zvornik to Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't mind if Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we go into this on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, we will -- we will go into it on Monday but I don't think it's an appropriate comment. If he wants to object he should give us the legal basis for it, not tell the witness -- the witness clearly knows what the time line is. He's brought here to share with us what that time line of the chain of custody of the documents are. And I think it's very inappropriate and quite candidly he's wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I have to stop --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he should read Mr. Vukicevic's statement again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But the legal basis is he's misstating the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll stop here. Mr. Bursik -- I was calling him Bursik now. Mr. Blaszczyk, thank you so much. The agreement is that we'll continue with him Monday morning. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think not, Your Honour. I talked to my colleague before and we would continue but now I can see this is going to be probably a lengthier cross than I expected and from talking to my friends Ms. Fauveau has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But can't we at least finish Mr. Ostojic's cross-examination on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could get an estimate but this could go on and on and on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much more do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read the transcript again, Your Honour I'll try to shorten it but given some of his answers and given that he does have additional information, I could be over an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'll let you discuss this amongst yourselves and then you tell us on Monday. Okay. Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Bearing in mind where we're up to, presumably the Court will give the normal warning to the witness not to discuss the case with anyone, in particular with the Prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You said not to discuss the case. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, the case needs to be discussed with the lead investigator on the case and that's what my friends, at least from the Beara team and I think from the Miletic team, have said is that they've got no problem with us speaking to the witness. We should be able to speak to the witness about anything other than his testimony. I mean we're obviously not going to talk about the questions or the answers or anything that's going on with the testimony on this topic, but we need to talk with the witness about the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Why does that need to be done prior to resolution of whether he's going to continue on Monday morning? In other words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's told you that for all intents and purposes he's the lead investigator in the Srebrenica case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in my submission, he's in the middle of giving evidence. If -- if he stops giving evidence now and doesn't resume on Monday then I say fair enough. But if he does continue on Monday morning, there's no reason for them to speak to him between now and Monday morning. That's how I put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think he should not continue Monday morning because when I spoke to my friends before, I said that the cross was going to be four -- the original cross estimate was four hours and they said it's going to be much less than that. And I asked if it was possible for him to just continue for a short while on Monday morning and the answer was yes. If this is going to go on throughout on Monday then we're not going to be able --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come down with our decision here and now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the position -- Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Josse, Mr. Nicholls, and everyone else, Mr. Blaszczyk's testimony stops here. And you will, of course, not be entitled to discuss with Mr. Blaszczyk the subject matter of his testimony. Of course, him being the lead investigator in the Srebrenica case, you will be entitled to discuss other matters with him. Monday we start with General Smith and we continue. Thank you. Have a nice weekend all of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
